Sophomoric

/sof-uh-MOR-ik/ - the stress falls on MOR · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Sophomoric means immature and overconfident; showing off like a juvenile.

The station's new morning hosts lean sophomoric — air-horn sound effects, fake accents, and a running bit about the traffic reporter's haircut.

Worked Example

The groomsman's toast was pure sophomoric swagger: three burrito stories, a nickname nobody had explained, and a bow held for applause that failed to arrive.

Sophomoric is more precise than 'childish' because it adds the strut: sophomoric humor or argument is immature AND pleased with itself — half-taught cleverness showing off. A toddler is childish; a nineteen-year-old quoting one philosophy lecture at Thanksgiving is sophomoric.

How Sophomoric Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

callow

callow: green and untested; sophomoric adds the strut of false confidence

immature

immature: simply not grown up yet, with no claim to cleverness

Antonyms

seasoned

seasoned: experience has sanded the showing-off away

dignified

dignified: carries itself with earned self-respect

How Strong Is It? — playful → juvenile → sophomoric

playful vs. sophomoric

playful vs. sophomoric: Playful is fun without fault — the mildest rung, nowhere near sophomoric, which turns the fun into a performance of how clever the joker is.

juvenile vs. sophomoric

juvenile vs. sophomoric: Juvenile humor is childish for its age, yet it stops short of sophomoric: add smugness — the wink that says 'admit it, I'm brilliant' — and the line is crossed.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of sophomoric.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — sopho-

Root — sopho-: wise (Greek sophos)

Root — mor-

Root — mor-: foolish (Greek moros)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: characteristic of

Put it together

Put it together: Sopho- (Greek sophos, 'wise') + mor- (moros, 'foolish') + -ic = characteristic of the wise fool. A sophomore is literally that contradiction: one year of learning, worn like a crown. The adjective bottles the type — just enough knowledge to perform, not yet enough to know better.

Use the root in a new word: philosophy

Use the root in a new word: philosophy: Philosophy — literally the love of wisdom — begins by admitting how little we securely know.

Word Choice

mocking / collegiate

Sophomoric is the reviewer's word for showing off that hasn't earned its swagger — pranks, puns, hot takes. 'Childish' scolds the age; sophomoric scolds the confidence. Its unit-mates carve up obnoxiousness precisely: moralistic lectures you, solipsistic forgets you, and sophomoric performs for you, certain you're impressed.
